## What

The `Language Models (Hybrid)` and `Granite Language Model Compatibility` jobs (and their mirrors) stop selecting tests out of `generation/` with `-m hybrid_model` / `-k 'granite-4.0-tiny-preview'`, and run whole coverage units instead. This is filter removal only: same tests, same markers, same replica counts, no sharding change.

## Old

```text
tests/models/language/generation/
├── test_hybrid.py          # Hybrid: -m hybrid_model -k 'not granite-4.0-tiny-preview'
│                           # Granite: -m hybrid_model -k 'granite-4.0-tiny-preview' (1 case of test_models)
└── test_gdn_sleep_wake.py  # Hybrid (via -m hybrid_model)
```

## New

```text
tests/models/language/generation/
├── test_granite_4_hybrid.py   # test_models[granite-4.0-tiny-preview], moved out of test_hybrid.py
└── hybrid/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── _hybrid_models.py      # test_models body + MAX_NUM_SEQS/ATTN_BACKEND; not collected
    ├── test_hybrid.py         # moved; Granite dropped from HYBRID_MODELS, test_models calls the helper
    └── test_gdn_sleep_wake.py # moved unchanged
```

| Job (key) | Old command target | New command target |
|---|---|---|
| Hybrid Shard %N (`language-models-tests-hybrid`, 2 replicas) + mirror + legacy `test-amd.yaml` | `generation -m hybrid_model -k 'not granite-4.0-tiny-preview'` + shard flags | `generation/hybrid` + shard flags |
| Granite Compatibility (`language-models-tests-granite-l4-compatibility`) + mirror + legacy `test-amd.yaml` | `generation -m hybrid_model -k 'granite-4.0-tiny-preview'` | `generation/test_granite_4_hybrid.py` |

## Notes

- **Coverage-neutral.** Static AST check: all 16 test functions and their decorators are unchanged except `test_models`, whose body moved verbatim into the helper; its 8 cases become 7 in `hybrid/test_hybrid.py` + 1 in `test_granite_4_hybrid.py`. Both files keep `hybrid_model`, so Extended Generation (`-m '(not core_model) and (not hybrid_model)'`), Standard, CPU and 2-GPU commands, which all discover `generation/` recursively, select exactly what they did before. `source_file_dependencies` are untouched; CODEOWNERS follows the move.
- **Hash assignment shifts.** The node IDs gain a `hybrid/` prefix, so `pytest-shard` places cases differently between the two replicas. Predicted from three recent `main` runs below: the heavy side moves from replica 2 to replica 1 with its slowest time within ±2 min.
- **Replaces drafts #56291, #56292, #56293, #56294 and #56313**, which are being closed as stale. Core/extended language filters and the coverage guard follow as their own PRs; sharding the still-slow Hybrid job is a separate Phase 2 PR sized from measured times.
- AI assistance was used (Claude Code). Checks run locally: static equivalence script, `ruff check`/`ruff format --check`, `py_compile`, `yaml.safe_load` on both pipeline files. `pytest --collect-only` and the GPU run come from the scoped validation build.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Predictions from per-case `_bk;t=` times in main builds [91217](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91217), [91208](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91208), [91196](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91196), re-hashed with the new node IDs.

| Job / replica | pytest (predicted) | running wall (predicted) | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Hybrid replica 1 (24 cases) | 25.5–30.1m (was 14.0–16.3m) | ~39–45m | ~13–15m, unchanged | mamba + causal-conv1d source builds before pytest starts |
| Hybrid replica 2 (13 cases) | 14.6–15.6m (was 24.9–31.7m) | ~28–31m | ~13–15m, unchanged | same |
| Granite Compatibility (1 case) | unchanged | unchanged (19–22m measured) | unchanged | same source builds |

- Worker-minutes: same replicas, same cases, same setup, so baseline → new is unchanged up to run-to-run noise; **extra ≈ 0 (within the 20-minute budget)**. Mirrors: same replica counts, predicted split also balanced as before, well inside their timeouts.
- Slowest Hybrid replica stays over the 20-minute target, as on `main`. Phase 1 deliberately leaves it slow; it is the Phase 2 candidate.

## Validation

Head `53c8d6a67e` (0 behind `main`). Builds: `ci` [91280](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91280), scoped to `language-models-tests-hybrid`, `amd-language-models-tests-hybrid`, `language-models-tests-granite-l4-compatibility`, `amd-language-models-tests-granite-l4-compatibility`; `amd-ci` [13633](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13633), with the legacy Hybrid and Granite steps released from their blocks.

**All 9 jobs passed on the first attempt, with no automatic retries.** Every job checked out `53c8d6a67e`.

**Coverage.** Each Hybrid shard collected 39 items from `generation/hybrid/`. That matches the 39 cases `-m hybrid_model -k 'not granite-4.0-tiny-preview'` selects on `main`. The split was 24 + 15 (13 passed + 2 multi-GPU skips), as predicted. Nothing is deselected any more. Each Granite job ran exactly `test_granite_4_hybrid.py::test_models[5-64-ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview]`.

**Primary lane, measured against `main` build [91274](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91274)**, which ran on this PR's base commit `22bbe3f102`:

| Job / replica | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause | `main` 91274 (pytest / wall) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Hybrid Shard 1 (24 cases) | 30.2m | 47.0m | 16.8m | mamba + causal-conv1d source builds before pytest starts (16.7m to session start) | 16.8m / 33.9m (17 cases) |
| Hybrid Shard 2 (15 cases) | 16.7m | 33.1m | 16.4m | same (16.3m to session start) | 31.8m / 47.6m (22 cases) |
| Granite Compatibility (1 case) | 3.4m | 18.8m | 15.4m | same | 3.9m / 18.8m |

- Worker-minutes: Hybrid 81.5 → 80.1 (**−1.4**), Granite 18.8 → 18.8 (**0**). Extra ≈ 0, within the 20-minute budget.
- Slowest Hybrid replica: 31.8m → 30.2m pytest, 47.6m → 47.0m wall. No worse. It is still over the 20-minute target, which is expected for filter removal and is the Phase 2 candidate.
- Against the prediction: Shard 1 came in at the top of the predicted 25.5–30.1m, and Shard 2 about 1m above the predicted 14.6–15.6m. As predicted, the heavy half moved from Shard 2 to Shard 1 because the node IDs gained the `hybrid/` prefix.

**Mirrors** (generated MI355 DPX mirror and legacy `amd-ci` steps): every replica passed. The mirror's slowest replica and total worker-minutes came in slightly below its own `main` baseline on the same base commit, well inside the timeouts. The legacy `amd-ci` steps have no comparable `main` baseline in hand, so for those I am reporting pass/fail only.

**Verdict:** coverage unchanged, runtime unchanged or better, and no extra cost on either lane.
